questions.question: Which of the following is considered the strongest and most secure password?
questions.hint: The best passwords use a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special symbols.

questions.question: If you receive an unexpected email asking you to click a link and enter your bank login details to 'verify your account', what is this called?
questions.hint: This is a common trick used by attackers to 'fish' for your private information.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)?
options: To make it faster to log into an account
To replace the need for a password entirely
To provide a second layer of security if your password is stolen
To encrypt the files saved on your computer
questions.hint: Think of it as adding a second lock to your door that requires a different key.

questions.question: Why is it risky to perform financial transactions on a public, unsecured Wi-Fi network?
options: The internet speed is too slow for banking
Your device battery will drain faster
Attackers can potentially intercept the data sent between your device and the router
Public Wi-Fi automatically deletes your browsing history
questions.hint: Unsecured networks lack encryption, meaning data travels in 'plain text' that others can see.

questions.question: Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which right allows an individual to request that a company delete all their personal data?
options: The Right to Erasure (Right to be Forgotten)
questions.hint: This right focuses specifically on the permanent removal of your data from a company's records.
